content.comment_body: Hello, I'm facing a basic issue connecting a [product_name] to my PC and then to AWS. When attempting connection, AWS shows a “DNS server is not accessible” error and suggests checking the [product_name] gateway’s internet connection. I tried adjusting both the PC network adapter settings and changing the [product_name] network configuration, but the device is not detected or doesn’t connect even when it is. Online research hasn’t helped much so far. [product_name] network settings: ip: 192.168.1.3 subnet: 255.255.255.0 gateway: 192.168.0.1 The router gateway is 192.168.1.15, and I tried configuring to match, but the problem persists.

The [product_name] and PC should be on the same IP subnet. Currently, you have: IP: 192.168.0.3 (assuming the previous number was a typo) Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0 gateway: 192.168.0.1 Meanwhile, your router’s IP is 192.168.1.15. Try changing the [product_name] IP to 192.168.1.3 and the gateway to 192.168.1.15.
Hello, Thanks for your help. I tried that, and now [product_name] Soft Comfort lists the device, but it still cannot connect. Is there something else I should check? Thank you.
Which [product_name] Soft Comfort version are you using?

If you’re using [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] and the device shows up in the list with both [product_name] and PC in the same subnet, I’m uncertain what’s wrong. Could you provide screenshots?
Hello, I’ve attached the screenshots below.
You should see a PC symbol in the network view. Click the settings icon for the PC to see the interface configuration. Please share a screenshot of this.
Try connecting the [product_name] directly to the PC using an Ethernet cable instead of going through the router.
The device is connected straight to the laptop via Ethernet cable; I might have omitted mentioning that. Are there any other settings I should adjust?
No specific suggestions. If you have antivirus software, try disabling it temporarily. Also, check your firewall settings.
Hello, I'll ask the system administrator to make these changes. Thank you for your assistance.
You didn't indicate whether you’re using a company network with your PC...
Yes, it’s a company device in the office. Sorry for not mentioning that earlier.
Then you should contact the network administrator. Certain ports on your PC may be closed, preventing communication between [product_name] and the PC.
I spoke to the administrator and changed the subnet to one that’s accessible, which resolved the issue. Thank you.
Glad to hear it worked. Thanks for updating us!

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered network connectivity issues while integrating a [product_name] device with a PC and AWS, receiving DNS server errors despite following standard network configuration practices. Adjustments were made to IP subnets and gateways, but connection remained unreliable until company network settings were addressed in coordination with IT support. Troubleshooting information from available sources was insufficient, and involvement of the IT administrator proved crucial.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated straightforward connectivity between the [product_name] device, PC running [product_name] Soft Comfort, and AWS, as well as clear troubleshooting instructions and network configuration guidance.
